column3: Universal prime connectivity needs orbit control, not a finite connectedness sweep; no tractable uniform orbit argument. Primary/current registry unreviewed.
Conditional on splitting and mirror-map hypotheses; period normalization and the smallest real field are indispensable. No algebraicity mechanism without primary definitions.

Primary Theorems 4.6 and 1.1 and concluding proofs give balanced trees on 2048 leaves with MAST 32 < sqrt(2048). Take c=1. Exact source scope, no new credit; auxiliary lemmas not independently audited.
An indefinitely extendible greedy procedure requires every switch and invariant to terminate for all stages. A billion steps cannot certify that. Algorithm body qualification missing.

Primary Conjecture 3.13 matches all d>=3 and fixed exceptional t. Genericity would require one nonzero determinant specialization for every d; source small-d Maple evidence does not provide this. No uniform factorization or tractable full-scope route established.
Need uniform logarithmic induced average degree for all triangle-free hosts; neighbourhoods themselves are independent. The loglog loss cannot be removed by an instance or elementary cut bound.

Requires every F, exponent alpha and positive blow-up r, with asymptotic constants. Tree/complete-bipartite instances do not bridge arbitrary F; even-cycle subcase already blocks simple embedding route.
Two-sided tight-in-probability bound across every weakly supercritical sequence requires cubic planar core cycle estimates and kernel transfer. Finite graphs do not decide it.
All ranks, sizes, coefficient indices and matroids required; sparse-paving bound is only a subclass. No coefficient-monotonicity bridge under relaxation for arbitrary matroids is available here.

Primary definitions identify C* with I(L,s,k) at k=L, admissible because L>=s+1. Theorem 3 gives strict inequality for N>=Gamma(s), hence weak inequality with M=Gamma(s) independent of L. Corollary 13 states the endpoint. Theorem 3 concluding proof read; injection dependencies not exhaustively replayed.

Primary Conjecture 6 is precisely the corrected three-case assertion. Section 4 proves it, with L=3,4 in Theorems 20,21 and L>=5 in preceding analysis. Selected proof passages read, not all injection/table computations audited. Not novel even if small certificates are recomputed.

Primary Conjecture 4.1 and Proposition 4.2 reduce it to filling each missing even gap below h(k-1) at the next primorial. CRT assignments can conflict; enumerating small k does not settle all k. No uniform gap-filling construction established.

Requires asymptotically almost sure approximate minimum-degree packing for every fixed p>1/2 and eta>0. Hamiltonicity alone supplies one cycle, not near delta/2 disjoint cycles; robust repeated-deletion control missing.

Ordered contribution is not defined by the literal text; need exact intersection-theoretic formula and degree domain before divisibility/nonnegativity can be tested. No primary qualification or proof bridge.

Source Conjecture 2 matches formula, but t=1 literal denominator vanishes and complete one-partite graph has no edges. This is a domain issue, not a credited refutation. For intended t>=2 no sharp universal inverse-Turan bound established.

Infinitely many return indices under every-power field-degree conditions needs number-theoretic control of new common divisors; finite recurrence sampling cannot certify infinitude. No primary-qualified uniform avoidance argument.

Need exact weighted index, root convention and minimizer definition. Local equal-size exchanges might fail across branches; first 80 branches do not imply all orders. No primary exchange inequality qualified.

Every 2-factor and every sufficiently dense even regular host require exact decomposition; source survey Conjecture 6.4 only supplies target. Absorption/robust decomposability not an elementary complete proof here.

Source notation Section 1.2 defines delta as minimum (k-1)-degree, whereas record explicitly calls it vertex degree. Source Conjecture 6.6 thus does not authorize solving the altered vertex-degree statement. Correction has zero credit; no promotion.

Successor arXiv:2201.04554v4 Theorem 1.1 proves high-girth Steiner triple systems for every sufficiently large n congruent 1 or 3 mod6. K_n triangle-divisible iff n is 1 or 3 mod6; triple blocks partition all pairs, hence edges into triangles. Choose successor g at least desired g to obtain required girth. Final proof pp50-52 read, not its full dependency tree.

Complete-host high-girth existence does not bridge all hosts with minimum degree at least 3n/4. Exact threshold plus simultaneous local sparsity needs more than successor complete-graph theorem; no tractable full-scope construction.

Exact-ID r304 historical disposition records a published positive-definiteness subsumption. Source Conjecture 11 and Theorem 1 cutoff read; no new nomination. Full older bridge not successfully retrieved in this run, so history exclusion is carried forward rather than independently re-established.

Literal defines s_r as minimum edge count, while title calls a degree bound; quantifier order also permits constants depending on parameters unless uniformity is imposed. Need primary definition before solving intended uniform bound; wording fixes earn zero.

All edge lists of size Delta+1 must work for every graph. Greedy edge colouring needs up to 2Delta-1; ordinary Vizing recolouring may use colours absent from lists. No source-qualified list-exchange bridge.

Primary Conjecture 1 matches every m>n>=1; Theorem 1 gives density/probability results for restricted trimming. Generic or almost-all irreducibility is not every endpoint. No uniform Newton-polygon/Galois certificate survives qualification.

Simultaneous list-forest and equitable capacity constraints for every graph and k require global recolouring. Degenerate/grid subclasses and unlisted equitable colourings do not cover arbitrary lists.

Need absolute quadratic dichromatic threshold for every n and arbitrary directed hosts. Exponential known threshold cannot be reduced by a fixed clique instance; no uniform disjoint directed linkage proof qualified.

Subdivisions must have internally disjoint long paths while preserving minimum outdegree in extracted core for every k. High outdegree alone does not make a greedy route disjoint; no full construction.
Need proper in-dominating X leaving minimum outdegree k in complement. Choosing a maximal random set may dominate but exhaust outneighbours; no uniform correlated selection guarantee established.

Bound actual arXiv:2008.13475v2 is Dilcher-Ulas on sparse polynomials, not the named harmonic-sum condition. Condition (4.1) of intended source remains unqualified. Record says refuted but this cannot supply a primary proof. No alternative-route fishing or novelty claim.

Primary Conjecture 6.6 lists the same four assertions. Prime q=2 in part (4) gives I(4)=2 versus part (2) I(4)=1, a literal endpoint conflict, not substantive discovery. Intended odd-prime restriction and complete group-family prior status remain gates.

Need host-independent constant for all hosts of max degree Delta and fixed F. Random edge sampling does not preserve F-freeness; complete-host extremizers cannot simply be pulled back without homomorphism obstructions.

Arbitrarily many minimum-degree vertices in Ramsey-minimal graphs for every 3-connected H requires attachment gadgets preserving both Ramsey and minimality. Existing sufficient subclasses do not bridge all H.

Primary paper defines arc-colouring, not literal vertex-colouring. Theorems 16,17 supply Eulerian and short-chord sufficient cases, not arbitrary Hamiltonian hosts. Read Theorem16 proof and start of17; no uniform bridge and no credit for correcting record wording.

Need absolute additive c for all girth-five planar graphs and all edge lists. Girth-four lower bounds and larger-girth upper bounds do not settle the boundary. No full discharging/list-extension mechanism.

Both dimensions must eventually have star chromatic index exactly six. A periodic six-colouring would need seam control for every large circumference and a lower bound; divisible-by-2-or-3 cases alone insufficient.
Need definitions of independent separations and embedding count C before exponent comparison. Degeneracy bounds alone ignore separator multiplicities. No qualified universal counting argument.

Primary Conjecture1 repeats the bound/equality. Literal includes crossing-zero trivial links, requiring a nontrivial-link domain convention before a zero-ball bound makes sense. This would be a wording/domain correction with zero credit. Intended nontrivial alternating equality needs a global lower-bound certificate, absent here.

Literal rho<1 does not state positivity, and rho=0 makes time exponent undefined. This is a domain gate, not discovery. Intended positive-rho aging requires equality-event continuity beyond weak convergence of the process; no full stochastic proof.

All 2<=k<l templates require uniform NP-hardness reductions; finite template instances or polymorphism calculations alone do not settle the family. Need precise relations and closest successor bodies before investment.

Asymptotic order in m with n sufficiently large needs exact order/uniformity of quantifiers. Improving both paper error sources to square-root scale is not supplied by a finite dynamic program; no source-qualified concentration proof.

Primary Conjecture8 matches arbitrary initial colourings and p threshold. Reusing the same graph creates dependencies between steps, so a one-step CLT cannot be iterated as independent samples. No full monotonicity/unanimity argument; not promoted.

All n and sufficiently large multiples d require uniqueness, not merely an explicit large independent set. Boundary monomials defeat naive residue-class counting; no uniform optimality/uniqueness certificate beyond reported n=3,4 instances.

All a,r,d,s and eventually n require comparing every weighted host against T(r,d). Definitions of Sigma, Pi and local multiplicities need primary qualification; d=0 instance does not bridge entropy optimizers for d>0.

Primary Definition5.1 and Conjecture5.2 require ideal equality over C for all arrangements with <=4 lines and arbitrary point multiplicities/d>=3. Corollary4 irreducibility is not equality of defining ideals; need radicality and saturation control, not finite sampled Groebner bases. No short universal certificate established.

Nested k,N limits for both fixed and arbitrary basepoints require asymptotic lower bounds. Equivalence to arithmetic Kakeya does not solve it; allowing zero common difference would change definitions and earn no credit.

Every increasing rational chain requires near-full logarithmic exponent, with limit N before k. Clearing denominators preserves a fixed finite pattern but not the needed quantitative lower bound. No full pattern-expansion mechanism.

Restricted positive-integer chains still quantify over every chain and all large N. Claimed equivalence with previous pattern problem is not a proof; no universal lower bound survives elementary collision counting.

For every n and pattern sequence, p tends to infinity before k; patterns may collapse modulo finitely many primes but that cannot refute the limit. Finite-field polynomial methods would need uniform degree/control for arbitrary U. No full-scope proof.

Every graph and target distribution require comparison with worst single-vertex target. Combining solutions for individual targets can reuse the same pebbles, so subadditivity does not supply the exact bound. No qualified universal rerouting invariant.
